scope: Standalone templating API; adding a host framework can provide separate application features.

ssr.note: Generates HTML from a template and supplied values on the server.

streaming.note: Execute writes incrementally to an io.Writer; execution errors may leave partial output. HTTP flush policy and Suspense are not provided.
streaming.label: io.Writer

suspense.note: The reviewed rendering API has no pending-UI/replacement protocol; the host application would need to provide one.

client.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

ssg.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

csr.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

serverOnly.note: The server evaluates templates and sends rendered output rather than the renderer implementation. This is not React Server Components.
serverOnly.label: Server templates

softNavigation.note: This standalone template/runtime renders content; navigation and page-transition lifecycle belong to a browser router or host application. Compatibility with a generic JavaScript library is not a built-in integration.

viewTransitions.note: This standalone template/runtime renders content; navigation and page-transition lifecycle belong to a browser router or host application. Compatibility with a generic JavaScript library is not a built-in integration.

redirects.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

serverData.note: This API consumes supplied template values; application data loading happens outside it.

clientData.note: Browser query lifecycle/cache APIs belong to a client library or application framework.

requestDedupe.note: Template/compilation caching is distinct from request-scoped application data deduplication.

persistentCache.note: Retaining application data or rendered pages across requests belongs to the host cache.

invalidation.note: Application data/page invalidation belongs to the host; recompiling a template is a different cache boundary.

isr.note: Regenerating deployed pages requires a host page cache/export pipeline.

apiRoutes.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

httpErrors.note: The reviewed renderer does not own the HTTP response. The host server must select 404/5xx, map routing/render failures, and decide when headers are committed. Displaying an error or fallback in rendered HTML does not establish the HTTP status.
httpErrors.label: HTTP host required

actions.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

forms.note: Templates can emit form markup; submission, validation, and feedback policy belong to the host application.

middleware.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

cookies.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

cssModules.note: CSS class-name compilation is a separate asset-build concern.

scopedCss.note: The renderer emits authored classes/styles; component-local CSS selector rewriting is a separate build concern.

tailwind.note: Tailwind can process authored templates through application configuration; the template renderer does not own that build.

cssInJs.note: Runtime CSS-in-JS compilation is outside this server template API.

images.note: Templates emit image markup; image resizing/conversion requires a separate asset pipeline.

fonts.note: Font downloading, subsetting, and fallback optimization require a separate asset pipeline.

scripts.note: Templates emit script markup; script scheduling and lifecycle policy belong to the host application.

assetPipeline.note: The reviewed standalone template API does not own an asset build or deployment pipeline. The host application or a separate build tool must version files, update template references, and configure browser/CDN cache headers.
assetPipeline.label: Host / build tool required

staticAssets.note: Serving files and assigning cache headers belong to the host web server.

metadata.note: Head tags can be templated directly; there is no structured metadata registry in the reviewed standalone API.

dynamicMetadata.note: Supplied values can populate head tags; request data loading and metadata composition remain application-owned.

metadataInheritance.note: Template inheritance/content composition is separate from a metadata-field inheritance contract.

metadataOverrides.note: A host head component or template block can override markup; structured field merge/clear rules are application-owned.

titleTemplates.note: Titles can use template expressions; ancestor metadata/title-template policy belongs to the application.

socialImages.note: Generating social-preview image bytes needs a separate image renderer/service.

sitemaps.note: XML can be templated, but route enumeration and a sitemap generator belong to the host.

robots.note: Text can be templated, but crawler-document publishing/configuration belongs to the host.

markdown.note: This is text/HTML templating; Markdown parsing and content-page integration require another tool.

collections.note: The host loads and validates structured content; the template API renders supplied values.

draftMode.note: Editorial preview authorization and published-cache bypass belong to the host application.

translations.note: Applications can supply translated strings/helpers; the reviewed renderer does not supply message catalogs.

localeRouting.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

localeFormatting.note: The host supplies locale-aware values or formatter helpers.

auth.note: Identity, login, and authorization are responsibilities of the host application.

csp.note: The host configures HTTP CSP headers and any nonce values passed into templates.

cspNonce.note: The HTTP application must generate a fresh nonce, set its policy and pass the value to authored tags. A template accepting attributes does not coordinate nonces for an application.

csrf.note: HTML escaping does not establish CSRF protection; the host must protect mutation endpoints.

environment.note: Server/client secret configuration belongs to the host application, not template evaluation.

types.note: The Go host is statically typed, but html/template resolves template paths/data at execution time. The reviewed template API does not establish compile-time template type checking.
types.label: Runtime template checks

hmr.note: Application rebuild/browser refresh orchestration is outside the renderer API.

cli.note: This renderer integrates with its language/build toolchain rather than supplying an application CLI.

bundleAnalysis.note: Production browser/server bundle inspection belongs to the host build toolchain.

unitTests.note: Applications test rendered output with their language test runner; no application test framework is supplied here.

e2eTests.note: Browser tests run against a host application, not a standalone template.

observability.note: Production request traces/metrics/logging belong to the host application.

errorHandling.note: Template errors are returned to the caller; application fallback/recovery UI is host-owned.

serverHosting.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

subpathProxy.note: The reviewed standalone template/runtime API does not coordinate a public URL prefix across routing, assets, links and proxy headers. That deployment behavior belongs to the host application or web framework.
subpathProxy.label: Host framework required

staticHosting.note: This review covers the standalone template API. Application routing, client activation, site generation, and server-function transports belong to the host application or an additional framework.

orm.note: ORM / query builder belongs to a server framework or external service, outside this standalone rendering API. This is not a missing template-rendering capability.

migrations.note: Schema migrations belongs to a server framework or external service, outside this standalone rendering API. This is not a missing template-rendering capability.

realtime.note: Real-time delivery belongs to a server framework or external service, outside this standalone rendering API. This is not a missing template-rendering capability.

xssEscaping.note: html/template performs contextual autoescaping for HTML, attributes, URLs, CSS and JavaScript. Trusted template.HTML/JS/URL types bypass parts of that policy; the template author is trusted.

htmlSanitization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific html sanitization contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

authorization.note: Authorization policies requires a host application or specialized integration beyond the reviewed template/runtime API. Emitting markup or using arbitrary host-language libraries does not establish this application-level contract.
